Prepare a spatio-temporal event dataset for semi-parametric Hawkes fitting

Source: R/prepare_events.R
prepare_events.Rd

Validates, cleans and reshapes a set of georeferenced events (e.g. crime records) and a study-region polygon into the flat structure used by the rest of the spHawkes EM pipeline: projected x/y coordinates, a numeric time index in days since start_date, and events restricted to region and to [start_date, end_date).

Usage

prepare_events(
  points,
  region,
  date_col,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  time_mark_step = 0.05
)

Arguments

points

An sf object with POINT geometry (one row per event).

region

An sf/sfc object with POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON geometry describing the study area (e.g. a city or district boundary).

date_col

Name of the column in points holding the event date (character scalar). The column may be Date, POSIXct/POSIXlt, or a string parseable by as.Date(). Date-times are converted to calendar dates in their own time zone (their tzone attribute, or the session's time zone if they have none), so an event at 20:00 on a Friday in Chicago stays on that Friday.

start_date

Start of the study period. If NULL (default), the earliest event date is used. Coerced with as.Date(), or, for a date-time, converted in its own time zone as for date_col.

end_date

Last date for selecting events, exclusive (events with date >= end_date are dropped). If NULL (default), the day after the latest event is used. Coerced as for start_date. The modelled study period always ends the day after the last event kept (TT), whatever end_date is. A later end_date is used only to label outputs, such as the printed study period and the date axis of plot_event_summary(), and a message says so.

crs

Target projected CRS (anything accepted by sf::st_crs(), e.g. an EPSG code) that both points and region are transformed to before any distance/kernel computation. If NULL (default), the CRS of region is used, and points is transformed to match. Both the resulting points and region CRS must be projected (linear units), not geographic (long/lat) — an informative error is raised otherwise, and a warning if the projected units are something other than metres (see the Units section below).

time_mark_step

Step (in days) used to build the time.marks grid returned in the output; default 0.05 matches the original script.

Value

An object of class "semihawkes_events", a list with elements:

events

A data.frame with columns coorx, coory, date, days (numeric days since start_date), and month (calendar month, 0-indexed, i.e. January = 0).

region

region, transformed to the working CRS.

crs

The working sf::st_crs() object.

start_date, end_date

The resolved study-period bounds. end_date labels outputs; the model uses TT.

TT

The modelled study horizon in days, max(days) + 1: the period runs from start_date to the day after the last event.

time.marks

Numeric grid seq(0, TT, time_mark_step).

n_input, n_outside_region, n_outside_daterange, n_kept

Counters describing how many input rows were dropped and why, for a quick sanity check on any new dataset.

Units

Every distance in this package — kernel bandwidths, cell_size, trigger window distances, triggering-kernel grid extents — is expressed in the linear units of the working CRS, and every default was chosen for a metre-based projection. A geographic (longitude/latitude) CRS is rejected outright, because degree-valued distances would be silently meaningless. A projected CRS in feet or kilometres is allowed but warned about, since the defaults will then be wrong by a large factor: usable, but only if you set every distance argument explicitly.

Examples

# `sim_events` / `sim_region` are simulated data shipped with the
# package; see `?sim_events`.
ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date")
print(ev)
#> <semihawkes_events>
#>   Study period : 2021-01-03 to 2024-01-01 (TT = 1093.0 days)
#>   Events kept  : 375 / 375 input rows
#>   Dropped      : 0 outside region, 0 outside date range
#>   CRS          : EPSG:32717

# Restricting the study period drops events outside it, and reports how
# many were dropped and why.
ev_2022 <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date",
                          start_date = "2022-01-01",
                          end_date   = "2023-01-01")
print(ev_2022)
#> <semihawkes_events>
#>   Study period : 2022-01-01 to 2023-01-01 (TT = 365.0 days)
#>   Events kept  : 113 / 375 input rows
#>   Dropped      : 0 outside region, 262 outside date range
#>   CRS          : EPSG:32717
